claims.title: DESI DR2 BAO: hint of evolving dark energy

claims.statement: DESI DR2 BAO combined with CMB and type Ia supernovae prefers w0waCDM (w0 > -1, wa < 0) over LambdaCDM at 2.8-4.2 sigma depending on the SN sample.

quantities.ours: -8.01 (reading B, omega_bc = omega_b + omega_c); -6.59 (reading A, with omega_nu)

updates: 2026: DES-Dovekie SN recalibration lowers the DES-SN combination from 4.2 to ~3.2 sigma (Popovic et al., arXiv:2511.07517).
2026-07: DESI DR2 Lya full-shape gives 2.7 sigma (DESI+CMB) and 3.2 sigma (with SNe) (arXiv:2607.27410).
open_questions: How much of the preference comes from the w0-wa parametrisation versus binned w(z) or Gaussian-process reconstructions?
Leave-one-tracer-out and leave-one-SN-sample-out sensitivity of the signal.
claims.notes: Verified against arXiv abstracts in plan 002 (cosmology agent report, 2026-11-11). Milestone M1. Study 002 (2026-11-14): BAO-only and no-CMB rows reproduced, compressed-CMB row conditionally reproduced; full-CMB and DES-SN5YR rows are out of scope (full Planck/ACT likelihoods; 53.5 MB covariance above the download limit). The compressed prior reproduces when its omega_bc mean is read as omega_b + omega_c (-8.01) but not with omega_nu added (-6.59); the referee pointed out that the split may lie within the (unmeasured) theta_* calibration systematics, so the convention is left open (T-022). Study 002 R2-CAMB (2026-11-16): with theta_* from CAMB (anchored and raw) the R2 verdicts are unchanged (Delta chi2 shifts -0.002 to -0.125), so the split is robust to the theta_* calibration and R2 depends on the omega_bc convention itself, which only a primary source can settle. Referee (2026-11-16, post hoc, verified): the prior's source cmbant/PlanckEarlyLCDM gives omega_b + omega_c = 0.14143; DESI's 0.14208 adds omega_nu, so reading A is the faithful source prior and A gives about -6.6, not -8.0; how DESI's code applied the mean is open (T-030). R2-CAMB-RD (2026-11-18, T-030, pre-registered): with theta_* and r_d both from CAMB the verdicts are unchanged (A -6.49 / -6.60, B -7.90 / -8.03), so the remaining ~1.4 under reading A is not from the r_d formula; DESI's configuration was not found in public sources. T-041 (2026-11-18, post hoc): DESI's public DR2 chain configuration feeds the compressed CMB likelihood ombh2 and omch2 with omch2 = omm h^2 - mnu/93.14 - ombh2, which indicates that the mean is compared with omega_b + omega_c (reading B; the likelihood source is not public, so an internal constant omega_nu cannot be excluded); the prior mean itself is 0.00065 above the source chain's omega_b + omega_c (open).

H0 CCHP TRGB, 11 JWST calibrators, Pantheon+
Same host shift with a host-level random effect (REML tau 0.077 mag; 5 log H0)

open_questions: Is the CCHP-SH0ES difference a calibrator-host selection effect? (Study 003, post-data host labelling: in R22's data the CCHP hosts lower H0 by 0.073 +/- 0.033 mag in 5 log H0, and on those hosts Cepheids and TRGB agree to 0.01 mag; the host labelling was amended after the first run. The 2.2 sigma uses C-propagated errors; random 10-host subsets show 1.33 times more scatter, placing the CCHP set at the 4.7th-5.7th percentile, about 1.7 sigma empirically (the subset spread is itself uncertain), where the pre-registered table would read no significant effect.) Update 2026-11-16 (R2-RE, pre-registered): with a host-level random effect the shift is -0.062 +/- 0.040 mag (1.5 sigma), not detected; robustness to single hosts open (T-032). Update 2026-11-18 (R2-RE-ROB, pre-registered): the null is sensitive to one host, N5584 (without it tau 0.031, and the full-data host step under that tau gives z' -2.04); tau not clearly unusual under the null (p = 0.07), the 1.33 random-subset spread is (p = 0.02); referee (post hoc, verified with an approximate check): N5584 (SN 2007af) carries all three signals, and without its rows the host shift is not detected under either covariance (z -1.63, -1.50); explicit treatment registered as T-039. Update 2026-11-18 (R2-RE-N5584, pre-registered, T-039): removing N5584 (36 hosts) leaves calibrator scatter consistent with C (null p 0.34 for tau, 0.36 for the subset spread; pre-registered reading 'attributable to N5584'; read post hoc only as consistent with one outlying host, because the null ignores the selection of the most extreme host; confirmed as the pre-registered reading of the selection-aware test R2-RE-SEL, T-042, 2026-11-20: p 0.24 for tau, 0.24 and 0.14 for the spread; referee, post hoc: low power against diffuse host scatter, a post-hoc spread-drop statistic points towards one host but no single-outlier model was simulated, T-048) and the CCHP selection at the 8.5th percentile; a Student-t host effect (nu = 4, variational EM) down-weights only N5584 (weight 0.39) and gives z = -1.38: the null holds under both treatments (method spread of z about +/-0.3, never reaching -2). Whether N5584's SN 2007af or its Cepheid distance is off is not identified by the data; the literature favours the SN.
claims.notes: Milestone M2. Study 003 R2-RE (2026-11-16): with a host-level random effect estimated by REML (0.077 mag), the CCHP host shift is 1.5 sigma and the pre-registered table gives no host-selection effect detected; the random effect removes the excess random-subset scatter (spread 1.33 -> 1.005). R2-RE-N5584 (2026-11-18): the excess calibrator scatter is consistent with one outlying host (N5584; also with the selection of the most extreme host simulated, R2-RE-SEL, T-042, a test with little power against diffuse host scatter, T-048); removing or down-weighting it keeps no host-selection effect detected (z -1.38 to -1.63).

open_questions: Minimal UV burstiness / star-formation efficiency needed at z ~ 12-15.
claims.notes: Milestone M8. Detection is established; the interpretation of the excess is contested. Study 006: the size of the excess depends strongly on the pre-JWST baseline (calibration-dependent across 72 model variants); the counts are two sources with Poisson errors only (cosmic variance, the effective area and the bin drawn around the detections are open gaps). The referee showed that 1 sigma in phi*, M* or alpha flips the sigma_UV verdict (phi* -1 sigma also brings the model within 3x of N26's baseline), and that a z ~ 8 dust correction raises the ratio and flips the sigma_UV verdict. T-025 (2026-11-16, pre-registered posterior calibration on binned z ~ 8 LF data): the excess over N26's baseline is robust to the LF calibration uncertainty (P(higher) >= 0.994 in all four fits; ratio 16-84% 7.5-14.2 in the primary fit), while the sigma_UV overlap with N26 stays borderline (P = 0.96, 0.86-1.00 with sigma_cal); both conditional on the fiducial model ingredients. T-036 (2026-11-18, pre-registered R3-POST2 with sigma_cal sampled, Poisson brightest bins, gamma >= -1): the excess stays robust (P = 0.99); the sigma_UV overlap is calibration-uncertain (P = 0.92), and the referee (post hoc) showed the data carry no information on sigma_cal, so P is set by the lower edge of its prior.

studies.title_zh: 宽双星：低加速度下是牛顿引力还是 MOND？
studies.question: In a clean Gaia DR3 wide-binary sample rebuilt server-side to the quality standard of Cookson et al. 2026, does the median scaled relative velocity stay flat with r_sky/r_M (Newton) or rise by ~20% beyond the MOND radius?
studies.question_zh: 在按 Cookson 等 2026 的质量标准、于服务器端重建的干净 Gaia DR3 宽双星样本中，缩放相对速度的中位数随 r_sky/r_M 保持平坦（牛顿），还是在 MOND 半径以外升高约 20%？

scale.note: Gaia DR3 wide binaries: velocities analysed to 150 pc (main sample 130 pc); the velocity-free R5 pair search to 250 pc; no lower distance cut (the nearest Gaia stars are at ~1.3 pc)

studies.title: M9 NANOGrav 15-yr GWB: power-law amplitude and spectral index from the KDE free spectrum
studies.title_zh: M9 NANOGrav 15 年引力波背景：由 KDE 自由谱拟合幂律振幅与谱指数
studies.question: Does a laptop refit of the NANOGrav 15-yr KDE free spectrum agree with the power-law amplitude and spectral-index statements of Agazie et al. 2023 (ApJL 951 L8), and how does the amplitude overlap with the SMBHB-population prediction of the companion paper L37?
studies.question_zh: 在本机用 NANOGrav 15 年 KDE 自由谱重拟幂律，振幅与谱指数是否与 Agazie et al. 2023（ApJL 951 L8）的陈述一致？振幅与姊妹论文 L37 的 SMBHB 群体预测重叠多少？

scale.note: pulsar-Earth distances of the NANOGrav 15-yr pulsars, 0.16-6.45 kpc (best estimates of the VizieR B/psr snapshot of the ATNF catalogue, 2017, 2,536 pulsars, defaulting to TC93 DM-based distances, for 55 of the 67; the 12 newer pulsars are not in that snapshot); the background's sources (supermassive black hole binaries) are cosmological

studies.title: M8 z ~ 14 galaxies: number density and the UV scatter a constant-efficiency model needs
studies.title_zh: M8 z ≈ 14 星系：数密度，以及恒定效率模型所需的紫外弥散
studies.question: Does the z = 14-15 number density that Naidu et al. 2026 infer from two spectroscopically confirmed galaxies follow from their counts and volume, how does it compare with an independent constant star-formation-efficiency halo model, and how much UV scatter would that model need?
studies.question_zh: Naidu 等 2026 由两个光谱确认的星系推出的 z = 14–15 数密度能否由计数与体积得到？与独立的恒定恒星形成效率晕模型相比如何？该模型需要多大的紫外弥散？

scale.note: z ~ 14-15 volume (comoving 10.3-10.45 Gpc, Planck18) and the z ~ 7-8 comparison luminosity functions (8.7-9.1 Gpc)

targets.name: MoM-z14
targets.note: Spectroscopically confirmed galaxy at z = 14.44, one of the two galaxies behind N26's number density at z = 14-15, which the study reproduces.
targets.note_zh: 光谱确认的 z = 14.44 星系，是 N26 在 z = 14–15 的数密度所依据的两个星系之一；本研究复现了这一数密度。

targets.name: JADES-GS-z14-0
targets.note: Spectroscopically confirmed galaxy at z of about 14.2-14.3, the other galaxy in N26's z = 14-15 count, and the only one in the Harikane et al. 2025 z ~ 14 bin (context, R4).
targets.note_zh: 光谱确认的星系，z 约 14.2–14.3，是 N26 在 z = 14–15 计数中的另一个星系，也是 Harikane 等 2025 z ≈ 14 箱中唯一的星系（背景，R4）。

studies.title: M10 GWTC-4.0 BBH mass spectrum: the 35 Msun feature and the event sample
studies.title_zh: M10 GWTC-4.0 双黑洞质量谱：35 M☉ 特征与事件样本
studies.question: Does the 153-event BBH sample of the GWTC-4.0 population paper follow from the public event lists, and does its claim of a feature at 35 Msun establish a steepening only, or an over-density?
studies.question_zh: GWTC-4.0 群体论文的 153 个双黑洞样本能否由公开的事件列表重建？它关于 35 M☉ 特征的结论能推出的是变陡，还是过密？

scale.note: comoving distances (Planck18) of the binary black holes, z 0.06-1.06; luminosity distances (posterior medians) 0.29-7.3 Gpc

studies.title: M3 S8 tension: DES Y6 3x2pt vs CMB parameter difference and multi-probe summary
studies.title_zh: M3 S8 张力：DES Y6 3x2pt 与 CMB 的参数差异及多探针汇总
studies.question: Do the public DES Y6 chains reproduce the 2.6 sigma (S8) and 2.2 sigma (S8-Omega_m) DES-CMB parameter differences, and does the paper's no-substantial-evidence conclusion follow from them?
studies.question_zh: 公开的 DES Y6 链文件能否复现 DES 与 CMB 在 S8 上 2.6σ、在 S8–Ωm 平面上 2.2σ 的参数差异？论文"没有实质证据表明不一致"的结论能否由此推出？

scale.note: DES Y6 lens and source galaxies (mean bin redshifts 0.31-1.16; comoving ~1.3-3.8 Gpc, Planck18; the redshift distributions extend beyond the bin means) and, separately, the CMB (~13.9 Gpc); a combined, not contiguous, range

survey.name: DES Y6
survey.note: about 5,000 square degrees of the southern sky; the CMB comparison (Planck 2018 + ACT DR6 + SPT-3G) is all-sky (Planck) with partial ACT/SPT coverage

studies.title: M6 Milky Way outer rotation curve: Keplerian decline, mass and systematics
studies.title_zh: M6 银河系外区旋转曲线：开普勒式下降、质量与系统误差
studies.question: Does the published Gaia DR3 rotation curve of Jiao et al. 2023 reject a flat curve at 3 sigma and imply a Milky Way mass of about 2 x 10^11 Msun, and how robust are both to Jeans-modelling systematics and to the halo extrapolation?
studies.question_zh: Jiao 等 2023 发表的 Gaia DR3 旋转曲线能否以 3σ 拒绝平坦曲线、推出约 2 × 10¹¹ 太阳质量的银河系质量？两者对金斯建模的系统误差与晕的外推有多稳健？

scale.note: distance from the Sun (the Atlas axis) implied by the published rotation-curve bins at Galactocentric radii 5.3-27.3 kpc (E19, O24, J23) with R0 ~ 8.2 kpc: bins span the solar circle, so the lower end is nominal (0.1 kpc), and the far side reaches at most R + R0 ~ 35 kpc; the virial radius (~110-120 kpc) is only extrapolated

survey.name: Gaia DR3 (+APOGEE)
survey.note: published rotation-curve tables built from Gaia DR3 disc stars (J23, O24) and APOGEE + Gaia (E19); no sky data fetched here

studies.title: M5 Milky Way thick disc: early formation from subgiant ages
studies.title_zh: M5 银河系厚盘：由亚巨星年龄看早期形成
studies.question: Does the published LAMOST/Gaia subgiant age catalogue of Xiang & Rix 2022 reproduce its thick-disc onset at about 13 Gyr, the split of the age-metallicity plane at 8 Gyr and the tight old-disc age-metallicity sequence, and how much of each depends on the absolute age scale, the error model and the sample selection?
studies.question_zh: Xiang & Rix 2022 发表的 LAMOST/Gaia 亚巨星年龄星表能否复现厚盘约 13 Gyr 前开始形成、年龄–金属丰度平面在 8 Gyr 处分开以及老盘紧致的年龄–金属丰度序列？各项在多大程度上依赖绝对年龄标尺、误差模型与样本选择？

scale.note: LAMOST/Gaia subgiants at Galactocentric 6 < R < 14 kpc and -4 < Z < 6 kpc (90% within 7.2 < R < 10.4 kpc and -1.2 < Z < 2 kpc); no heliocentric range is given: toward the anticentre, which the LAMOST footprint favours, R = 14 kpc with Z = 6 kpc is ~8-9 kpc from the Sun (an estimate under that assumption; a purely geometric bound for the full volume would be ~23 kpc); XR22 state no lower distance, the 0.1 kpc start is nominal

survey.name: LAMOST x Gaia
survey.note: LAMOST spectroscopic footprint (mostly northern sky) with Gaia parallaxes
